response.sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) AS avg_ALP, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_HCT FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-') GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX ORDER BY avg_HCT IS NULL, avg_HCT DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A patient qualifies if at least one Laboratory row has U-PRO and RA both exactly equal to the text '-', and the qualifying row itself is not required to be part of the averages.
The averages use all of the patient's Laboratory rows, as the request says 'across all of their lab records', with AVG ignoring NULL values.
Patients with lab rows but no Patient row are excluded, because the request says to list only patients present in the Patient table (the inner join does this).
Missing average HCT values sort last by ordering on the 'avg_HCT IS NULL' flag before the descending average.
